claims.text: Enhanced structural and chemical stability in high-entropy nanoalloys is primarily governed by synergy between high configurational entropy and local lattice strain.
Random elemental mixing and atomic-size mismatch create local lattice distortions.
Configurational entropy and local lattice distortions raise the energy barrier to phase separation.
Local lattice distortions reduce atomic diffusion at elevated temperatures.
The as-synthesized nanoalloys are single-phase random solid solutions with uniform nanoscale particle size and disordered atomic distributions.
The proposed thermal protocol uses steps at 400°C, 500°C, and 600°C.
The proposed control is a binary or low-entropy alloy with similar composition and particle size prepared and thermally treated under identical conditions.
Using an inert or reducing atmosphere isolates diffusion and phase-transformation behavior from oxidative interference.
Randomly distributed multiple elements produce local lattice distortions and compositional fluctuations.
Local lattice distortions and compositional fluctuations kinetically hinder diffusion.
The multielement atomic structure thermodynamically stabilizes the mixed phase against segregation.
High configurational entropy lowers the free-energy difference between disordered and segregated states.
Lattice strain caused by atomic-size mismatch creates kinetic barriers to atomic movement.
The combination of entropic stabilization and strain-induced kinetic barriers delays phase separation and chemical degradation at elevated temperatures.
Relative to the binary-alloy control, the high-entropy nanoalloys will retain a single-phase random solid solution with minimal phase separation or ordering up to about 600°C.
Relative to the binary-alloy control, the high-entropy nanoalloys will exhibit lower effective diffusion coefficients.
The predicted stabilization is limited to inert or reducing atmospheres and temperatures near or below 600°C.
Above approximately 600°C, high-entropy effects may no longer prevent significant phase separation.
The limiting temperature and relative contributions of configurational entropy and lattice strain depend on elemental combination and particle size.
Phase separation, ordering, or atomic diffusion in the high-entropy alloy at or below the corresponding onset in the control would falsify the proposed mechanism.
